liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dark Star** (3 reviews): Dark Star is called possibly the best of the five played that year; The Weather Report Suite into Dark Star into China Doll run is singled out as the highlight [6][7][13]
- **Bertha** (1 review): Bertha is spare, opening with simple drums and piano; Weir enters later alone in the left channel [9]
- **Loser** (1 review): Loser is singled out as a particularly strong version [8]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): Scarlet Begonias is singled out as a particularly strong version [8]
- **Playin' In The Band** (1 review): Playin' runs about twenty minutes and wanders widely; Jerry is inspired, with strong Weir and Billy interplay [12]
- **Weather Report Suite Prelude** (1 review): The Weather Report Suite into Dark Star into China Doll sequence is described as a rare combination [6]
- **Not Fade Away** (1 review): Not Fade Away is praised highly [13]
- **Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad** (1 review): Not Fade Away into Goin' Down the Road is called possibly the best of 1974 [12]

## The recordings

- **gd74-05-14.sbd.murphy.1823.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 25 songs; 184 min; rated 4.41/5 by 70 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says Jerry is weakest in the mix, suggesting the soundman lost part of his performance; Reviewer finds the sound crisp, with Jerry's guitar playing prominent [16][17]
- **gd1974-05-14.163764.sbd.miller.patched.sirmick.flac16**: soundboard; 23 songs; 196 min; rated 5/5 by 4 [2]
- **gd1974-05-14.163756.aud.lamarre.vernon.sirmick.flac24**: audience recording; 23 songs; 177 min [4]
- **gd1974-05-14.sbd.miller.114462.flac16**: soundboard; 23 songs; 195 min; rated 4.28/5 by 36 [3]

## Around the show

- Reviewer who lived in Montana was surprised the band rocked the place so hard [13]
- A audience member shouts a request for Tie a Yellow Ribbon just before Playin' starts, audible on the tape [15]
- Show has circulated less than other well-known 1974 shows, which may explain why it is underrated [6]
- The Bertha's plain earnestness recalls the version on the Skull & Roses album [9]
- May-June 1974 shows are all excellent, with some of the band's most unusual and exciting jamming [11]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd74-05-14.sbd.murphy.1823.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Taped by Bob Murphy on MSR; lineage cassette, DAT, CD-R, then shn [1]
- **gd1974-05-14.163764.sbd.miller.patched.sirmick.flac16**: transferred by This is a patched version of shnid 114462; source: Set 1: SBD -> Master Reel -> Cassette -> Dat (48k) Set 2: SBD -> Master Reel -> Dat (44.1k) [2]. Also: Patched version of shnid 114462; China Doll tape flip patched from shnid 163755; only set 1 pitch corrected [2]
- **gd1974-05-14.163756.aud.lamarre.vernon.sirmick.flac24**: taped by Unknown; transferred by Matt Vernon, SirMick; source: Audience Cassettes (up to El Paso described on j-card as 7th gen and the rest of show 8th gen) from collection of Doug Lamarre [4]. Also: Audience source with many faded or clipped tracks, patched using shnid 114462 where parts were missing [4]
- **gd1974-05-14.sbd.miller.114462.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Set 1: SBD -> Master Reel -> Cassette -> Dat (48k) Set 2: SBD -> Master Reel -> Dat (44.1k) [3]

## Art and photos

- Poster by RareVinyl.com: [Grateful Dead Dave's Picks Volume 9: Harry Adams Field House, U. Of Montana, Missoula, MT 5/14/74 US 3-CD set](https://eu.rarevinyl.com/products/grateful-dead-dave-s-picks-volume-9-harry-adams-field-house-u-of-montana-missoula-mt-5-14-74-us-3-cd-album-triple-set-r2541133-848359) [19]
